clue.definition: a small sign that helps you decide something, like a word or a mark in a message

score.definition: a number made by adding up points

threshold.definition: a line a number has to reach; at or above it, one thing happens, below it, another

training.definition: the way a program works out its own settings from many examples, instead of a person setting them by hand

filter.definition: something that lets some things through and holds others back

junk.definition: messages you did not ask for, such as adverts and tricks, kept apart from your main messages

program.definition: a list of exact steps that a computer follows

inbox.definition: the place where the messages you want arrive

pixel.definition: one tiny square of a picture on a screen or in a photo; the computer keeps it as one number, or three numbers for colour

grid.definition: squares laid out in rows (across) and columns (up and down), like a page of squared maths paper

number-representation.definition: writing something, like a picture, a sound or a word, as numbers so that a computer can keep it and work with it

brightness.definition: how much light something gives out; in a grey photo, each pixel's number usually says how bright it is, from 0 (black) to 255 (white)

average.definition: add up some numbers, then divide by how many numbers there are; for 3, 6 and 9: 3 + 6 + 9 = 18, and 18 ÷ 3 = 6

dataset.definition: a collection of examples, each with its label, that a machine is trained on

label.definition: the answer a person attaches to an example, such as “1” or “7”, so a machine can be trained on it

sample.definition: a small part picked from a bigger group, used to learn about the whole group; it only works if it is like the whole group

bias.definition: in data, when some kinds of people or things are missing or rare, so a machine trained on it tends to work worse for them

accuracy.definition: how many answers are right out of all the answers, often given as a percentage: 3 right out of 4 is 75%

percentage.definition: a number out of 100, written with %: 50% means 50 out of every 100

token.definition: one piece of text that a computer reads at a time: a word, part of a word, or a mark such as a full stop

vocabulary.definition: the list of all the different tokens a model can use; each token is listed once

probability.definition: how often something happens, out of all the times it could; 3 times out of 4 is a probability of 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75

prediction.definition: a guess about what comes next, worked out from what happened most often in earlier examples

error.definition: a number for how wrong a model's guesses are; training tries to make it smaller (also called the loss)

model.definition: the counts or number settings a computer uses to make its guesses, worked out from examples

example.definition: one thing a machine learns from, such as one photo or one food, usually with its label

pattern.definition: something that repeats, or things that usually go together, which help you guess about new cases

rule.definition: an exact instruction for what to do in a situation, such as “if it is round and yellow, call it a mango”

learning-from-examples.definition: finding a pattern in many labelled examples and using it to label new things, instead of following rules someone wrote

fairness.definition: treating people so that no one gets a worse result for a reason that should not count, such as the language they write in

responsibility.definition: being the one who must answer for a choice and put it right if it goes wrong; for AI systems, this stays with people, not the program

hallucination.definition: when an AI system, such as a chatbot, gives an answer that sounds sure but is false or made up

anthropomorphism.definition: talking about something that is not human as if it had human thoughts or feelings, such as saying “the AI thinks”

ethical-framework.definition: a set of questions people use to decide what is right, such as “Which choice does the most good?” or “Which promises must be kept?”

chatbot.definition: a program you type or talk to, which replies with sentences built from patterns in the very large amount of text it was trained on

neural-network.definition: a program built from layers of neurons joined by weights; training sets the weights from examples

neuron.definition: in a neural network, a tiny calculator: it multiplies each number it receives by a weight, adds them up, and passes on one number

weight.definition: in a neural network, a number that says how much one input counts; training adjusts the weights to make the error smaller

layer.definition: a group of neurons in a neural network that work side by side and pass their numbers on to the next layer

noise.definition: small random wobbles in data that are not part of the real pattern

loss-curve.definition: a chart of the error after each step of training; when training goes well, it slopes down

underfitting.definition: when a network is too simple to catch the pattern, so its error is high even on its training examples

overfitting.definition: when a network follows its training examples so closely, noise included, that its error on new examples is high

generalisation.definition: doing well on new examples a network was never trained on, not only on its training examples
